subskill: Table-given line vs line of slope k; count k
prompt:
The table gives three values of the linear function f.
x | f(x)
-1 | -16
4 | 4
9 | 24
The function g is defined by g(x) = kx - 37, where k is a constant. For how many integer values of k from -1 to 14, inclusive, do the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) meet at a point that lies above the x-axis?
explanation: From the table, f increases by 20 when x increases by 5, so its slope is 4 and f(x) = 4x - 12. A point of the graph of f lies above the x-axis exactly when 4x - 12 > 0, that is, when x > 3. Setting g(x) = f(x): kx - 37 = 4x - 12, so (k - 4)x = 25. Treat k = 4 as its own case: the equation becomes 0 = 25, so the lines are parallel and never meet; k = 4 does not count. For k ≠ 4 the graphs meet at x = 25/(k - 4), and we need 25/(k - 4) > 3. If k < 4 the x-value is negative, so it fails. If k > 4, multiplying keeps the direction: 25 > 3(k - 4), so k < 37/3, about 12.33. The values k = 5, 6, ..., 12 work, so the answer is 8. Choice 14 comes from multiplying by k - 4 without checking its sign, which keeps every k from -1 to 12, including k = 4, where the lines never meet. Choice 10 tests whether the meeting point is to the right of the y-axis (x > 0) instead of above the x-axis. Choice 5 comes from a sign slip, (4 - k)x = 25, which makes the values k = -1 to 3 appear to work.
solve: const m=(4-(-16))/(4-(-1)), b=4-m*4; let n=0; for(let k=-1;k<=14;k++){ const a=k-m; if(a===0) continue; const x=(b-(-37))/a; if(m*x+b>0) n++ } return n

distractor_solve.5: let n=0; for(let k=-1;k<=14;k++){ if(k===4) continue; if(25/(4-k)>3) n++ } return n
distractor_solve.10: let n=0; for(let k=-1;k<=14;k++){ if(k===4) continue; if(25/(k-4)>0) n++ } return n
distractor_solve.14: let n=0; for(let k=-1;k<=14;k++){ if(25>3*(k-4)) n++ } return n

mechanism: above the x-axis means x > 3 on f
k = 4 gives parallel lines (no meeting point)
sign of k - 4 decides the inequality direction
quantity_asked: number of integers k from -1 to 14 inclusive for which the graphs of f and g meet above the x-axis

setup.i: f is a linear function given only by a table; g(x) = kx - 37 with slope k, so the intersection x-coefficient k - 4 vanishes at one k
setup.ii: the graphs of f and g intersect at a point above the x-axis
setup.iii: number of integer values of k in a stated range

5.why: The sign slip moves the window to the other side of k = 4, and the range is cut off at -1 on that side; the stem gives no way to see that the mirrored window is clipped.

10.why: Testing x > 0 (right of the y-axis) instead of f(x) > 0 changes the bound from x > 3 to x > 0; whether that loosens or tightens depends on the zero of f, which only the table reveals.

14.why: Multiplying 25/(k - 4) > 3 by k - 4 with no sign case keeps k = -1 to 3 and the parallel case k = 4; the stem does not show that the meeting point is at a positive x, so the side of this error is not readable.
